solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Restrained worker dealt a blow

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in a farmhand
to cuff someone is to hit them with the open hand

explanation.surface: A labourer who struck someone ends up held back, perhaps by the police.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone shackled at the wrists has been physically restrained.

clue.text: Nag writer

definitions.meaning: a hired horse, an old nag

explanation.surface: Someone pesters an author.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a worn-out horse for hire and a writer of dull, mercenary copy.

clue.text: Knight loads pasta

parts.note: N is the chess notation for knight
oodles means loads, a great quantity

explanation.surface: A knight piles on the pasta.
explanation.definitionFit: Noodles are strips of pasta or similar dough.

clue.text: Bug associated with ghost town in Sussex, we hear

parts.note: a ghost story is creepy, spooky

indicators.note: we hear signals that the town's name is spoken aloud

parts.note: Crawley is a town in West Sussex, near Gatwick airport

explanation.surface: Some insect is linked to a haunted town in southern England, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: A creepy-crawly is an informal word for a small insect or spider, a bug.

clue.text: Compliments cook imbibing coffee

indicators.note: imbibing means drinking in, so the drink goes inside

parts.note: to fry is to cook
a latte is a milky coffee

explanation.surface: Someone praises the chef as they sip coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: Flattery is excessive praise, a stream of insincere compliments.

clue.text: Musician Brian's horrified expression no more!

parts.note: Brian Eno is an ambient music producer
ugh is an exclamation of disgust

explanation.surface: A rock musician's appalled cry demands an end to it.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation 'Enough!' calls a halt, demanding that something stop.

clue.text: Dress to boast over

indicators.note: in a crossword, over can mean turned over, so the word for boasting is read backwards

parts.note: to brag is to boast

explanation.surface: Someone is told to show off their outfit all over again.
explanation.definitionFit: Garb is a noun for clothing or dress, especially distinctive attire.

clue.text: Excellent condition, being solvent

parts.note: ace means first-rate, excellent
tone is physical condition, as in muscle tone

explanation.surface: Being in fine shape financially, with money in the bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solvent' suggests having money; here it is the chemical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetone is a chemical solvent, used in nail varnish remover.

clue.text: Female marsh bird apparently showing resentment

parts.note: the bittern is a heron of reed beds and marshes
-ess is a feminine suffix, as in lioness

explanation.surface: A hen bird of the reeds looks embittered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apparently' admits the joke: a female bittern would be a 'bitterness' by analogy with lioness.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitterness is a feeling of anger at unfair treatment, a synonym of resentment.

clue.text: One working together with old film star and another caught out

parts.note: Gary Cooper, Hollywood star of High Noon

indicators.note: out tells us the cricket letter for caught is removed from the other performer

parts.note: another film star, i.e. an actor
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone collaborates with a veteran screen idol and a second performer who is caught out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' means another film star, ACTOR; 'caught out' removes its C to leave ATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A co-operator is a collaborator, a person who works jointly with others.

clue.text: Model of inebriety initially wallowing in gin

indicators.note: in places the opening letter inside the word for a trap

parts.note: a gin is a trap for animals, like a net

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A drunk is pictured wallowing in a glass of gin.
explanation.walkthrough: Gin here is the trap, not the drink, despite the drinking surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'as pissed as a newt' makes this amphibian the proverbial standard of drunkenness.

clue.text: Heartsick Matt almost frantic to get a new flame?

indicators.note: frantic means wild, so the letters are rearranged
almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the name is dropped

explanation.surface: A lovelorn man named Matt is desperate to find a new partner.
explanation.definitionFit: Lighting a fresh fire from a matchstick produces a flame; the question mark plays on the romantic sense of a new lover.

clue.text: Elude fielder

definitions.meaning: to give someone the ... is to escape them
a cricket fielder standing beside the wicketkeeper

explanation.surface: Someone dodges a cricketer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both escaping someone and a close catching position in cricket, next to the wicketkeeper.

clue.text: Daft to grip the dangerous crossing?

indicators.note: daft means crazy, so the following words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Is it foolish to take hold of something on a perilous crossing?
explanation.definitionFit: A high wire walked by a circus performer is a crossing with real danger; the question mark flags the playful description.

clue.text: Drunk's written about one in columns

indicators.note: written about means a word is set around another, enclosing it

parts.note: plastered is slang for very drunk
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A drunkard is profiled in newspaper columns.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilastered describes a building with pilasters, flat rectangular columns set into a wall.

clue.text: That is treatment keeping bridge pair vulnerable

indicators.note: keeping means holding something within, so the pair goes inside

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, that is
North and South are a partnership at the bridge table
a cure is a course of treatment

explanation.surface: A remedy that protects a couple of card players is weak.
explanation.definitionFit: Insecure and vulnerable are synonyms: both mean unprotected or open to harm.

clue.text: Rebuke English cricket side getting duck

parts.note: to wig is an old-fashioned word for to scold
the on side is one half of a cricket field, also called leg side

explanation.surface: An England batsman is told off for scoring nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck in cricket is a score of nothing, which the surface exploits.
explanation.definitionFit: The wigeon is a species of wild duck.

clue.text: Sycophant of distinguished person pricked by needle

indicators.note: pricked by means pierced, so the irritation goes inside

parts.note: Hon is short for Honourable, a title of a distinguished person
to needle is to anger or irritate

explanation.surface: A fawning follower of a VIP gets jabbed with a needle.
explanation.definitionFit: A hanger-on is a person who attaches themselves to someone important for advantage, a toady.

clue.text: Resistance shown in a fake religious community

indicators.note: shown in tells us the letter is put inside the other pieces

parts.note: a sham is a fraud or fake
R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Opposition is shown towards a cult that is a fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: An ashram is a Hindu religious retreat where a community lives around a guru.

clue.text: Sources supplying quicksilver writer

parts.note: Hg is the chemical symbol for mercury, quicksilver
wells are sources of water

explanation.surface: Springs supply mercury to an author.
explanation.definitionFit: H. G. Wells was the English author of The War of the Worlds.

clue.text: Fuel was great for cooking

indicators.note: cooking means fiddling or tampering, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some fuel was great for preparing food.
explanation.definitionFit: Water gas, made by passing steam over hot coke, is a fuel gas of carbon monoxide and hydrogen.

clue.text: Gentle old king has a double

parts.note: GR is Georgius Rex, King George
dual means double, twofold

explanation.surface: A mild former monarch has a lookalike.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentle slope or change is gradual, slow and moderate rather than steep.

clue.text: Put a stop to one born in Greek island hospital

indicators.note: in says the first pieces sit inside the island name

parts.note: Kos is an island in the Dodecanese
I is the Roman numeral one
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A baby delivered in a Greek island hospital halts something.
explanation.definitionFit: To put the kibosh on something is to quash it, the idiom here used as a verb.

clue.text: Became upset about intimate rubbing down

indicators.note: about tells us one piece surrounds the other
in a down-style reading upset means turned over, so the word is reversed

parts.note: got can mean became, as in got angry
to be well in with someone is to be on intimate terms

explanation.surface: Someone got upset about a close relationship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses the word for became, giving TOG; 'Became upset' misleads as a feeling, and 'rubbing down' is a noun for drying with a towel.
explanation.definitionFit: Towelling is the act of drying vigorously with a cloth, a brisk rub-down.

clue.text: Police force seizing a substance

indicators.note: seizing means grabbing hold of, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police

explanation.surface: London police confiscate some drug or other.
explanation.definitionFit: The meat of something is its substance or essential content.

clue.text: Bird that's surprising North America

parts.note: my! is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: A bird turns up unexpectedly in North America.
explanation.definitionFit: The myna is a starling from Asia known for mimicking speech.

clue.text: Part played in control experiment

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the following words

explanation.surface: Someone takes a part in a scientific trial with a control group.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor's role is the part they play.

clue.text: With Gore ousted by Republican, tyro usually worried me

indicators.note: worried means agitated, so the letters are rearranged
ousted by means replaced by, so one name gives way to the party letter

parts.note: Al Gore, the US vice-president

explanation.surface: A political novice was troubled when the Democrat Gore lost to a Republican.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping AL for R in TYRO USUALLY leaves TYROUSURLY, and 'worried' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a jocular way for a speaker to refer to themself, the first person.

clue.text: Ruin radio receiver, perhaps

definitions.meaning: to ... someone's hopes is to wreck them
a satellite or radio telescope ... is a receiver

explanation.surface: Someone wrecks a radio set.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for spoiling chances and a noun for a bowl-shaped aerial collecting signals.

clue.text: Friend with cold wrapped in fur

indicators.note: wrapped in means enclosed, so the chilly word goes inside the pal

parts.note: china is Cockney rhyming slang (china plate = mate) for friend
a chill is a cold

explanation.surface: A pal with a cold is bundled up in a fur coat.
explanation.walkthrough: China plate is Cockney rhyming slang for mate, so china means friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Chinchilla is the soft grey pelt of a South American rodent, prized as luxury fur.
